## Contract review brief — PR #37063 @ `7d7ca6db2425ef185280bf98952ac758a0ce1f37` (card #36422)

You review at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`. Render ONE `## Contract review` record on this head — its shape is
`node scripts/pm/record-recognisers.mjs --template` — with a PASS or FAIL verdict, and post it as ONE comment
on the PR or its card.

Inputs — these and nothing else:
  · card #36422: its body and EVERY comment (rulings and earlier records included)
  · PR #37063: its body, its file list, and the net diff against `main` at `7d7ca6db2425ef185280bf98952ac758a0ce1f37`
  · the check-runs on `7d7ca6db2425ef185280bf98952ac758a0ce1f37`: their conclusions ARE the gate verdicts
⛔ Not the dispatch order, ⛔ not the dispatching seat's own conclusions — this brief is adversarial by design.

Scope — the paths `reviewFace` returns as `hits` on this PR's file list: skills/objectstack-ui/rules/list-views.md;
  plus every file IN THIS DIFF that directly implements or enforces them — the gate that enforces a rule, the code
  a jsdoc or schema line describes, the validator a skill teaches — reviewed for agreement with the contract.
  Widen it freely, ⛔ never below `hits`; the record's `Scope:` line names the implementing files apart from `hits`.
  The rest of the diff (tests, unrelated modules, lockfiles, generated output, changesets) is the lane seat's
  ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`, exactly as a standalone PR of those files.
  ④ judges the `hits` files and those implementing files ONLY:
  lockfiles, generated output, changesets and prose elsewhere in the PR are not reviewed;
  code outside the diff is READ to judge them, never reviewed.

Security — if a `hits` path is under `skills/**` or `ui/skills/**` and the change teaches security, auth or permission
  behaviour the path name doesn't show, the record says so and the seat adopting the record adds the `security` label.
  The record says so on its `Security-touching:` line, and the arm lands on `no` alone: write `no` ONLY when no changed
  hunk teaches permission, sharing, credential, token, authentication or other security behaviour, else `yes`.

Rule change — if a `hits` path is under `.claude/**`: the PR body declares `Rule-change:` and you verify it against the diff.
  Write `Rule-change-verified: none` ONLY when no changed hunk alters what an agent may do without the maintainer
  (merge, bypass a check, change repository settings), what gets done and in what order (grading, dispatch, scope), or
  what must go to him (decisions, maintainer actions); process steps, scripts, wording, slimming and file moves are not rule
  changes. Write `ruled` ONLY when every such hunk copies the ruling the PR body quotes on its `Ruling-ref:` line — check the
  copy against the quoted words, do not re-rule it. Otherwise `yes`: the pull request then waits for the maintainer.

⛔ READ-ONLY. No worktree, no checkout, no build, no test run, no gate re-run, no ablation: the check-runs
   on the head already answered every derived gate family, and a local run costs more than it returns.
   If ONE probe is unavoidable, the record's `Local-runs:` line says `probe — REASON`; otherwise `none`.
   Scratch space is `/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-objectstack/177ababb-cccd-573a-a846-cda17d8e5bbd/scratchpad/pr-37063/` alone; nothing there you did not write this round is read.

Judge, in the record's own sections:
  ① Derived judgments — every accept-set and public-surface change the diff implies, each named right or wrong.
  ② Semver level — the changeset (or `skip-changeset`) matches what the diff publishes, and the `Clause-②:` line.
  ③ Boundary flags — every dev flag and every `open_questions` entry answered, or escalated.
     On every face, SQL push-down: a new id materialisation or in-app join where SQL could push down is a
     finding unless a reason is given (AGENTS.md, Prime Directive 5: SQL first).
  ④ Design judgment — for EVERY `hits` file: does the change hold against the code it cites and the
     scenario it is accepted against? A skill file against the card's eval prompt and the spec it teaches
     on `main`; a schema file against the ruling or ADR it implements and its first consumer; an ADR
     against its first consumer and its execution plan. For EVERY implementing file in the diff: does the
     code agree with the contract, sentence by sentence? Read the cited code in the live tree, and try to
     break the design.
     Grade each finding must-fix, should-fix or nit — a nit has no effect on correctness or the contract.
     A must-fix is a FAIL; a must-fix or should-fix earns a delta review of its fix; nits alone end the round.
     Spell a must-fix or should-fix with its id and grade, `S1 (should-fix) — …`, and a clean round as
     `No must-fix, no should-fix.`: the queue guard reads a graded finding as OPEN on this head and
     refuses the record; the delta record names those it closes by id alone, `S1: closed`.
     A nit is fixed only on the prose faces, or left as an accepted deviation or a follow-up card: a fix
     anywhere else moves the head, and this record no longer covers it.
     ⛔ Judge the tree, never the PR body's account of it.
Sign `Implemented-by:` with the dev's branch and `Reviewed-by:` with your session id — the value is the FIRST
thing after each colon.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `7d7ca6db2425ef185280bf98952ac758a0ce1f37`
Local-runs: none
Scope: skills/objectstack-ui/rules/list-views.md + none
Security-touching: no
Rule-change-verified: none

PR #37063 (card #36422), one commit on main `a68b475bbc`. Read: the card body and its five comments, the PR body, the file list, the net diff, the 44 check-runs on the head, and `packages/spec/src/ui/view.zod.ts` on main. Nothing built, run or re-run.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Accept set: unchanged, right.** The diff is one skill file and one changeset; no schema, lint or renderer path moves. `Metadata-protocol: none` is right: nothing a metadata author can write changes.
- **The example's keys are accepted on main, right.** `KanbanConfigSchema` declares `summary` (view.zod.ts:2513, `KanbanLaneSummarySchema`, optional), `showFieldLabels` (2528) and `hideEmptyFields` (2537), both `z.boolean().optional()`. `{ type: 'sum', field: 'estimate_hours' }` is the `sum` arm of the discriminated union (2407-2413). The block is `os:check`; `Type Check · consumer gates` (runs `check:skill-examples`) is success on the head.
- **`summarizeField` is still accepted, right.** view.zod.ts:2499 is a plain `z.string().optional()`, no `retiredKey` tombstone, no conversion. The skill stops teaching it and does not call it refused or removed, so nothing narrows and no narrowing arm is owed.
- **Published surface that moves: `@objectstack/skills` text only, right.** `rules/list-views.md` 17788 → 17775 bytes, 4447 → 4444 tokens under the row's ceiling of 4448; no ratchet row moves. `Type Check · source gates` (token ratchet, skill links) and `Lint · docs & code guards` (identifier liveness) are success.
- **Other `summarizeField` teaching in the skills: none, right.** On main the one hit under `skills/` and `ui/skills/` is the example line this diff replaces (card to-do 2 has nothing else to align).
- **Check-runs on the head: 44, of which 28 success, 16 skipped, none failed, cancelled, neutral or pending.** Skipped, all expected for a skills-prose diff: the path-filtered UI and docs jobs (`Build & E2E UI`, `Lint UI`, `Type Check UI`, `Build UI Deps`, `Plan Test UI shards`, `UI Published Artifacts`, `Build Docs`, `Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL)`, `Dogfood Verify CLI`, and the two unexpanded matrix parents for Test UI and the Dogfood Regression Gate), the two opt-in jobs (`Packed-tarball smoke`, `18.x upgrade harness`), the merge-group jobs (`Queue verdict`, `Borrowed queue verdict`) and the `Schedule gate`. `Check Changeset`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `PR-body guards`, every `Lint ·` and `Type Check ·` job, `Build Core` and `Test Core` are success.

### ② Semver level

`'@objectstack/skills': patch` matches what the diff publishes: skill wording in a released package (`packages/skills/package.json`), protocol kind `none`, so `patch` is the level and `skip-changeset` would have been wrong. The Clause-② declaration reads `no` with no arm on both carriers (PR body and changeset body), and that is right: no accept set widens or narrows. `Check Changeset` is success.

Not graded (changesets are outside ④): the changeset says the example "sets `showFieldLabels` and `hideEmptyFields` with their defaults (both `true`)". The example writes both as `false`; the comments carry the default. The sentence ships in the changelog and can be read the other way.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Dev deviation, no eval case (drafted, dropped on overlap with open PR #37043):** accepted for this head. The card's acceptance asks for the example and for no contradiction with the spec, not for a case. **Escalated to the seat:** the report names the owed case with `carrier: none`, and `Fixes #36422` closes the only card that carries the two `Skills-docs: follow-up owed` lines (#36411, #36857). The "evals exercise it" half of that debt needs a card of its own, blocked by #37043, before ACCEPT. N1 and N2 below can ride on it.
- **Dev deviation, local gates run at the pre-amend commit, five families not measured locally:** answered by the head's check-runs, all success or an expected skip.
- **Dev deviation, amend before the first content push, no force push:** no effect on the reviewed head (one commit, parent `a68b475bbc`).
- **Dev deviation, PR body layout (seat signature line before the closing line):** `PR-body guards` is success; no contract effect.
- **Dev deviations, commit trailers and draft state with no label:** the seat's lane. The PR is still a draft.
- **`open_questions`:** empty. **`security_findings`:** none, and none found here.
- **Security read, hunk by hunk.** No hunk adds or alters a statement about permission, sharing, credentials, tokens or authentication. The new note leaves out the spec's two permission clauses (aggregates run "under the reader's permissions"; "a field the reader may not read shows no figure") and so teaches no permission behaviour. The closest call is the toolbar-search hunk: it shortens the sentence about the `$searchFields` ingress gate, a control ADR-0061 files under D5 Security. The words that stay are byte-for-byte main's; the words that go ("the whole search box, for every user and every term: no result at all") describe how far a bad entry breaks search, which the heading and the table still say. The diff teaches nothing new or different about that gate. The seat can overrule this one call if it reads "changed hunk" as any hunk whose surviving line mentions the gate.
- **SQL push-down:** no code in the diff. The note teaches that the four aggregates are computed by the query, which agrees with SQL first.

### ④ Design judgment

No must-fix, no should-fix.

**(a) The nine cuts.** Each removed passage is still said in the file at the head; no rule an author needs is gone.

| # | Removed | Still said at the head | Holds |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| 1 | search example comment "No `searchableFields` → the toolbar searches everything the object allows" | table row "key omitted: scans the object's full allowed set" (line 200) | yes |
| 2 | comment "This list only: search the reference number and the subject line" | "narrows that set for this one list" (160) and the `searchableFields` line itself (174) | yes |
| 3 | "The full dropdown / tabs / toggle range applies only to page lists / `interfaceConfig.userFilters`" | "`tabs` is page-only" in the same bullet (148); the range is still listed at 125-130 | yes, see N3 |
| 4 | "the whole search box, for every user and every term: no result at all" | heading "One bad entry 400s EVERY search on that list" (192) and the two `400 INVALID_FIELD` rows | yes |
| 5 | "errors, not warnings" | "Both diagnostics are **errors**: `os validate` fails the build" (205) | yes |
| 6 | comment "no search box" | "To remove the search box, toggle the affordance instead" (207) | yes |
| 7 | "one lane per option" on `groupByField` | `lanes` note "Omit it to draw every option in its own order" (281); "one empty lane per option" (303) | yes |
| 8 | "the default `list` and every other view untouched" | "a NEW `listViews` entry that coexists with the views the object has" and "Never satisfy an add by retyping `list` (or an existing named view)" (292-296) | yes |
| 9 | gantt comments "task bar start" / "task bar end" | the key names, the "required" sentence (319-320), "bar label" on `titleField` | yes |

Cut 7 also removes a comment that was untrue of its own example, which sets `lanes` and so does not draw one lane per option.

**(b) The board example and note against `KanbanConfigSchema` on main.** Every clause has a source sentence, and none contradicts the describe text.

- `summary: { type: 'sum', field: 'estimate_hours' }`, "each lane's foot statistic": describe text "The statistic each lane shows at its foot" (2514). Right.
- `showFieldLabels`, "default true: cards name each field": "Omit for true (names shown); false shows the values alone" (2529). Right.
- `hideEmptyFields`, "default true: cards drop an empty field": "Omit for true (left out); false keeps the field with an empty value" (2538). Right.
- The six values `none`, `count`, `sum`, `avg`, `min`, `max`: the six arms of `KanbanLaneSummarySchema` (2394-2435), `field` required on the last four. Right, and it covers the card's scope addition (#36857).
- "computed by the query over every record of the lane, not only the loaded cards": "each computed by the query" (2516) and the schema note "never added up over the cards a lane has loaded" (2383-2385). Right.
- "Known gap: over a lookup field or in a grouped view, `sum` covers one fetched page and the other three show nothing": "in a list view, lanes over a lookup field or a view with grouping ... `sum` totals the records handed in, one page, unmarked, and the other three show nothing" (2518-2520). Right in substance, see N2.
- "`summary` overrides the older sum-only `summarizeField`": "Takes precedence over summarizeField" (2521); `summarizeField` describes itself as "Field to sum" (2499). Right.

Tried to break it: the example type-checks against `ListView` (consumer gate green); the column-level `summary: 'min'` comment "plain enum value, not an object" (line 66) is scoped to a column and does not collide with `kanban.summary`; the eval case that expects "beside the untouched default `list`" is still taught after cut 8; the page key that cut 3 drops is taught in `rules/navigation.md` (132-153).

- N1 (nit): nothing in the new lines says the three keys are optional. The old comment on `summarizeField` opened with "optional"; the new `summary` comment does not, and the note never says that omitting `summary` shows no statistic (spec: "Omit to keep summarizeField's sum, or no statistic without it"). The two booleans are written with the non-default `false`, so an agent that copies the example ships cards without field names and with empty rows unasked. The comments do carry "default true", and the example already wrote optional, non-default `lanes`. Card to-do 1 asks for the defaults of all three; the acceptance line does not. Left as is on this head; carry it on the eval follow-up.
- N2 (nit): "Known gap: over a lookup field" has no subject. It follows "`sum` / `avg` / `min` / `max` of a `field`", so it can be read as the summary's own `field` being a lookup. The spec says "lanes over a lookup field". The file's own idiom ("A board over a field added in the same change") supports the intended reading. "lanes over a lookup field" is 6 bytes against 17 bytes of headroom. Left as is on this head; carry it on the eval follow-up.
- N3 (nit): cut 3 removes this file's only mention of `interfaceConfig.userFilters`, the place "page-only" points at. The rule stays in the bullet and the key is taught in `rules/navigation.md`. The removed sentence was also loose: `ObjectUserFiltersSchema` on main accepts the deprecated `toggle` on an object view (view.zod.ts:5913), so only `tabs` was ever page-only. Accepted as is.

Nits only; the head is not moved.

1. **Shape.** 2 files: `skills/objectstack-ui/rules/list-views.md` (the board example writes `kanban.summary`, `showFieldLabels`, `hideEmptyFields`; one note on the six lane statistics, the spec's known gap and `summary` over `summarizeField`; nine same-file restatement cuts pay for it), one `@objectstack/skills` patch changeset. Every clause of the example and note checked against `KanbanConfigSchema` in `packages/spec/src/ui/view.zod.ts` by the contract review.

4. **Contract review.** PASS 7140561770 at this head (brief 7140539603), `Security-touching: no` — the one close call (the toolbar-search hunk shortens main's sentence about the `$searchFields` ingress gate) teaches nothing new about the gate; the seat zone keeps `no`. Nits N1–N3 accepted.
5. **Out of scope → filed.** The owed eval case (dropped by the dev on overlap with PR #37043) and nits N1/N2: filed #37074 (`Blocked-by: #37043`), so `Fixes #36422` does not close the last carrier of the #36411 / #36857 eval debt.
6. **Landing.** Tier S on the low-risk skills arm with this record; the zone lands it.
